substantiveness.reason: The target is a real conditional bound, not a tautology. Its conclusion (formal/nightstream-fprime/tests/EvidenceTargets.lean:290-304) bounds the actual accepted-terminal mass Pr[target.Holds] by the returned-advice mass plus, for each j < depth, marked hash-collision mass + goodActive_j - g(Q_j, goodActive_j) + deltaFS(Q_j) + weakLoss + testError + arity.total * adaptive MSIS success. AdviceReturned is a real extraction event: run returns advice of length iteration whose forward fold reaches zi (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Export/Stage1/HyperNovaHistoryProbability.lean:29-33). The accepted event is the wide terminal relation (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Export/Stage1/Wide/TerminalSecurity.lean:73-75). The real-success mass is not a free scalar: it is proved equal to the goodActive mass (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Export/Stage1/HyperNovaVisitedAcceptance.lean:206-222). The MSIS term is the computed adaptive reduction's success, and the factor is PaperProfile.arity.total = 17 (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Spec/Folding/Nifs/PaperProfile.lean:67). The premises can be satisfied: the FS model is one real inequality (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Lifecycle/Nifs/WideFiatShamir.lean:108-112); clocks, bounds, summability and the depth bound are ordinary data. With g(Q,p)=p and a small deltaFS the conclusion is a knowledge-soundness bound that does not follow without the FS premise. The theorem is closed by the fail-closed #audit_axioms and #evidence_closed checks (formal/nightstream-fprime/tests/EvidenceTargets.lean:311; formal/nightstream-fprime/tests/EvidenceAcceptance.lean:17; formal/nightstream-fprime/tests/AxiomAudit.lean:7-15). I did not run the build; I rely on the stated passing build and axiom audit at this commit.

The terminal reaches the same verifier: target.Holds is Stage1.Terminal.HoldsFor target.relation target.ajtai target.context target.program (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Export/Stage1/Wide/TerminalSecurity.lean:73-75); its outer transition reads only setup.verifierKeys (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Spec/HyperNova/Construction2/Paper.lean:576-590), so the narrow Lifecycle.setup used by HoldsFor (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Lifecycle/Stage1/Terminal.lean:71-82) injects no narrow NIFS verifier; the fresh opening yields Stage1.Wide.Relation.StepHoldsFor, whose NIFS verifier is verify (PiRLC.Wide.Key.key ...) (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Lifecycle/Stage1/Wide/Relation.lean:19-33, 45-47). For Wide.selected this key is SetupBinding.nifsKey = FixedPoint.key (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Export/Stage1/Wide/SetupBinding.lean:75-76; formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Export/Stage1/Wide/FixedPoint.lean:100-103). Interactive side: PiRLC.Wide.Key.key is { ProductionKey.key relation ajtai with piRlcResponse, piRlcResponseValid } (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Lifecycle/PiRLC/Wide/Key.lean:34-38). piRlcAlgebra, the Challenge subtype, arity, params, statement, piRlcSemantics and the piDec fields are therefore shared by definition, and response_valid puts every wide challenge in the same challengeValid set (Key.lean:19-21). A grep of the interactive modules (SupportedExtraction, InteractiveComposition, SupportedContinuation, WeakExtraction, InteractiveOutput, InteractiveAgreement, BindingProbability, AdaptiveBinding*) finds only the fields arity, params, piRlcAlgebra, piRlcSemantics, statement, piDecAlgebra, piDecEvaluationArity, piDecPublicInputSplit, constantLaw and kPositive, and whole-key uses only through PaperWeakOutput, PaperStrongInterface and PaperCompositionAgreement, which contain no piRlcResponse, verify or piDecAttempt. originalSuccess is the uniform-challenge weak continuation (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Lifecycle/Nifs/InteractiveComposition.lean:40-79), and weakLoss = arity.total / |Challenge| over the shared set (77-79). So the mixing is sound as stated: ProductionKey.key on the interactive side names only fields that the wide key shares, the only law difference (wide map versus uniform challenges) sits inside deltaFS as FIAT_SHAMIR_MODEL.md:108-111 states, and Lean asserts nothing about that difference beyond the premise. The source event is key-independent: SourceReturned is equivalent to Lifecycle.TerminalHolds target.relation target.ajtai (formal/nightstream-fprime/NightstreamFPrime/Export/Stage1/HyperNovaSource.lean:207-214). target_meaning.reason: For every wide target, every ordinary State and Tape type, every initial PMF of terminal statements and envelopes with counters at most depth, and every fixed operational extractor data, if each guarded real experiment at the actual visited laws satisfies the approved wide-key FS transfer with shared g and deltaFS, then Pr[wide terminal accepts] <= Pr[the reverse walk returns advice of the right length that folds z0 to zi] + sum over j < depth of (Pr[first marked state-hash collision at visit j] + active_j - g(Q_j)(active_j) + deltaFS(Q_j) + weakLoss + testError + 17 * Pr[computed adaptive MSIS reduction succeeds at visit j]). This is literally the registered criterion (scripts/lean_graph/HYPERNOVA_LINEAR_SECURITY.md:15-27) and the obligation gap (obligations.json:373). The only semantic change since the old target is the intended one: the retired narrow terminal and real event are replaced by the wide terminal and wide real event, for every wide target. The statement does not claim FS instantiation, MSIS hardness, collision resistance of the state hash, a work bound or a deployed security level; those remain explicit or external, as its docstring says (EvidenceTargets.lean:217-219).

findings.text: The instance binders, weakLoss and the interactive experiment name ProductionKey.key, not the wide key. This is sound because the wide key overrides only piRlcResponse and piRlcResponseValid, and the interactive chain reads neither. A reader can mistake it for use of the retired sampler; FIAT_SHAMIR_MODEL.md:108-111 explains it.

The real adversary at visit j is defined analytically: it outputs the terminal's proof and child witnesses exactly on goodActive visits, which depend on the earlier history walk and marks. That p_real = Pr[goodActive] is exact by construction. Whether this experiment is an admitted adversary within the declared Q (FIAT_SHAMIR_MODEL.md:29-37) is external to Lean, as it was before the port.

The bound is parametric in g and deltaFS. With a large deltaFS or g = 0 the premise holds and the conclusion is weak. This is inherent to the approved parametric boundary (FIAT_SHAMIR_MODEL.md:60-65), not a defect of the target.
LowNormInvertibility (SuperNeo Theorem 8 for this ring) stays an explicit premise, as in the old target. It is not discharged in this tree; if it were false the target would be vacuous.
The marked state-hash collision mass is not bounded here. Poseidon2 state-hash collision resistance is a separate obligation.

The target quantifies over every Wide.Target, which is stronger than the selected package. Wide.selected takes compiled and parts as free parameters, and no Lean theorem instantiates the target at it. The link from the deployed package to Wide.selected belongs to the production review.
The owner note still names branch nico/f-prime-constraints-cuda-formal; the work is on nico/pirlc-wide-sampler-integration.
